engagement.judgement: Scored same with source_calls_it partial (status table: partial agreement). The 2011 assay read proliferation and cytokines; Rudulier read tetramer frequency and chemokine receptors on the same cells, so the match is on the system, not the identical readout. Readout is direct: the peptides' target cells examined ex vivo. A contra reading (the stated hypothesis of an altered chemokine-receptor profile mostly failed) is defensible; hence low confidence.

The 8 x 6 nmol escalation also failed, so this is not a too-low target. Decision 16 does not apply: the chamber stated no tolerability margin. No NCT found for the Phase 3, so registry_date is null. ALK press release 2017-09-14 announced the Phase 3 primary met (TCS -39.6%, p<0.0001) before the chamber dose-finding was published (Couroux epub 2018-11-22); dose counts the same drug's own earlier patient result, so retrodiction by post-dating. dose.quote: For the BPS, absolute (relative) differences from placebo were 3.02 (40%) for TCS, 1.32 (37%) for DSS, and 1.58 (49%) for DMS (all P < .0001).

Decision 16: the chamber stated 12 DU was well tolerated and the field reached it without that toxicity, so margin_stated true. Same ALK tablet as the sibling tile's 'birch pollen allergen extract'; re-verified here, not copied. Sits on the 'other' strip, so the peptide contra of 2016 does not block it. Ruling 2026-11-09 (retrodiction by post-dating, dose: same drug's own result): ALK's 2017-09-14 release made the Phase 3 result public before the chamber's dose pick, so same -> retro and 2019 -> 2018.

Ragweed-SPIRE never went to field (this release stopped its dose-ranging preparation) and ALK's cat SLIT chamber study was never published, so neither scores.

safety.confidence_note: Model side: Hafner 2013 WAO J congress abstract (WISC 2012, Dec 2012; PMC3643727) of the Cat-PAD chamber study: 'Cat-PAD was safe and well tolerated and improved TRSS.' Patient side: press release 2016-06-20 (tier 5); SAE counts from the registry results posted 2018-05-14.
safety.note: Chamber abstract stated Cat-PAD was safe and well tolerated, a scored safety prediction; the 1,407-patient intradermal field Phase 3 was well tolerated.
safety.quote: The treatment was well tolerated with a highly favourable safety profile.
safety.judgement: Safety split by modality (intradermal peptide vs sublingual tablet). Scored same, not other, because the comparison is absence of harm, not a shared harm. Ruling 2026-11-09: a passing tolerability claim is a safety prediction; the chamber study's own sentence (Hafner 2013) now carries the model side, settling the checker's unverified verdict.

safety.magnitude_basis: nature and severity of the most frequent adverse reaction; frequencies not compared
safety.confidence_note: Couroux 2019 full text (PMC6588091) and Biedermann 2019 abstract (epub 2019-01-15). Phase 3 identified by EudraCT 2015-004821-15 only. ALK press release 2017-09-14: Phase 3 'treatment was well-tolerated by patients'; chamber paper epub 2018-11-22, so the tablet's own patient result came first (safety retrodiction).
safety.note: Chamber tolerability (mild-to-moderate local oral reactions; Couroux online 2018-11-22) was public after ALK reported the Phase 3 well tolerated (2017-09-14): retro by post-dating.
safety.quote: The most frequently reported treatment-related adverse events were mild or moderate local reactions related to sublingual administration.
safety.reason: Chamber safety public after field result
safety.judgement: Paired comparison between the chamber dose-finding (Couroux 2019: 'the most frequently reported adverse reactions being the local reactions in the oral cavity of mild-to-moderate severity') and the field Phase 3 of the same tablet. Sits on the 'other' strip. Ruling 2026-11-09: for safety only the same drug's own earlier patient result counts; the tree tablet's own Phase 3 tolerability was public 2017-09-14, before the chamber paper, so same -> retro, 2019 -> 2018.
